76ba859a0a.q: What percentage of a business owner's time and labor is typically unaccounted for when calculating company value?
76ba859a0a.a: Many business owners fail to recognize how many hours and full-time equivalents they personally contribute to the business. Gregory gave the example of a highly productive florist in Louisiana who was so efficient she could complete 10 designs while average florists completed 4-5, requiring 2 to 2.5 people to replace her when she sold. Owners often don't realize the void created when they leave, especially when seasoned entrepreneurs can make decisions in 20 minutes that would take a newcomer three hours.

975440127d.q: Why do serial entrepreneurs often sell their businesses before scaling to large team sizes?
975440127d.a: Gregory's client Mohamed in the tech space has sold four businesses because he loves small dedicated teams working hard on a product but dislikes when he needs an HR department and CFO. He typically reaches a certain scale, then sells so he can move on to new projects rather than manage large organizational structures. His preference is working with 3-8 people rather than 25.

e2f5065ab5.q: What is the main mistake business owners make when assessing their company's marketability?
e2f5065ab5.a: The biggest lie owners tell themselves is not recognizing how many hours and full-time equivalents they personally contribute to the business. They see strong financial returns but fail to disclose that a buyer would need to hire multiple people to replace their personal productivity, expertise, and decision-making speed. This creates a valuation gap between what the tax returns show and what a new owner can actually replicate.
